cim: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for short-to-medium range weather prediction
cim_eredeti: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for short-to-medium range weather prediction
szoveg_eredeti:
Short-to-medium range weather prediction is a crucial component of decision-making for energy and disaster management and preparedness. However, conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) faces computational costs when increasing spatial resolution to capture localized phenomena or expanding ensemble size to improve probabilistic skill. In this Review, we summarize the development and application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for short-to-medium range weather prediction (AIWP) during 2015–2025, providing a holistic evaluation of the landscape and recommendations for best uses and future research priorities. New AIWP models implemented in the field can overcome computational cost barriers and resolution constraints of NWP by learning from decades of reanalysis and observational data rather than solving complex differential equations. Integration through post-processing, emulation of physical parameterizations, data assimilation and development of full AIWP models have already demonstrated performance equivalent to conventional NWP with a fraction of the computational cost. Challenges of AIWP models include dependence on training datasets, maintaining physical consistency, accuracy of forecasting extreme weather and lack of trust in their operational use. Future research priorities must focus on developing hybrid approaches that preserve physical constraints; using curated datasets to ensure forecasts are robust, trustworthy and explainable; and fostering interdisciplinary collaborations to handle increasing climate variability and extreme events.
